Reward designThe shape the reward encodes

Reward as a function of the count and the signed error. The full-credit ridge at error = 0 and the decay walls both widen with the count — an off-by-one is fatal at gt=3 but forgiven at gt=100.

HeadlineOld exact-match vs new graded

Exact-match is scale-blind and sparse: mean reward collapses 0.73 → 0.065 from gt=1–4 to gt≥100 and zeros 48% of pairs. The graded reward stays flat ~0.67 across every magnitude and turns the dead-zero mass into a smooth learning signal.

DecompositionLeniency vs gradient (band-only isolates them)

graded=false keeps the scale-aware band but drops the decay, splitting the gain: the band alone lifts 0.516→0.585 (leniency), the decay adds 0.585→0.709 (gradient) and removes the zero cliff (41.5% → <1%).

RecommendationTraining-arm shortlist (prepared, not launched)

A 4-lens agent panel + two adversarial verifiers (all numbers reconciled to summary.json) converged on this ladder. Every arm runs the identical config and differs only in reward_kwargs.counting_*. Budget rule: 2 runs → arms 1–2; 3 → +3; 4 → +4.

#armroleHydra overridesexperiment_name
1graded_defaultreference(none — bit-identical to shipped)counting_reward_graded_shipped
2exact_matchbaseline+…counting_rel_tol=0.0 +…counting_rel_band_cap=0.0 +…counting_graded=falsecounting_reward_exact_baseline
3sigma030treatment+…counting_rel_sigma=0.30counting_reward_sigma030
4band_onlycontrol+…counting_graded=falsecounting_reward_band_only
Read under GDPO/GSPO: the group-relative advantage cancels the reward level — only within-group spread trains. A high mean isn't disqualifying; flat regions (mass at 0, or a full-credit plateau) are. Judge every arm on counting-domain exact-accuracy, not blended reward.
sigma030 caveat: a wider σ awards ~0.97 to gt=100/pred=110 and can teach "roughly right is fine" on large counts. If it games in training, swap in the hack-resistant +…counting_rel_tol=0.0 (arm reltol0). Do not launch multi-GPU without Chris.
